title: The Ophiuchus DIsc Survey Employing ALMA (ODISEA) - III. The evolution of substructures in massive discs at 3-5 au resolution
question: What are the incidence, properties, and evolutionary sequence of substructures in the brightest massive protoplanetary discs in the Ophiuchus star-forming region at 3-5 au resolution?

what.value: 1.3 mm low-resolution fluxes for sample targets

evidence.quote: The $\alpha_{IR}$ values taken from (cite: evans2009) and the SED classifications (as discussed above) are also listed in Table [\[t:sample\]](#t:sample).

what.value: High-resolution ALMA data and stellar properties for 5 Ophiuchus DSHARP targets

evidence.quote: Five of them (SR4, Elias 2-20, DoAr 25 and Elias 2-27 and Elias 2-24) are part of the DSHARP ALMA Cycle-4 program (cite: Andrews2018) and were already observed at $\sim$5 au resolution.
For these DSHARP objects, we adopt the stellar properties (measured and derived) listed by (cite: Andrews2018).

recipe.goal: Derive stellar properties and classify SEDs
recipe.method: Classify YSOs using 2-20 um IR slope alpha_IR and mid-IR morphology; fit extinction A_V and luminosity using J-band bolometric corrections and BT-Settl model photospheres; infer stellar masses and ages from BT-Settl evolutionary tracks (or statistical durations for embedded sources).
key_parameters: Class I: alpha_IR > +0.3; FS: +0.3 > alpha_IR > -0.3; Class II: -0.3 > alpha_IR > -1.6; Class III: -1.6 > alpha_IR; TD/PTD threshold: [3.6]-[4.5] = 0.25
assumptions: Temperature scale from Pecaut & Mamajek (2013); extinction law from Fitzpatrick (1999) with NIR corrections by Indebetouw et al. (2005); statistical ages <= 0.5 Myr for Class I and <= 1 Myr for Flat Spectrum sources

recipe.goal: Fit disc geometry, measure disc radii R_90%, and calculate dust masses
recipe.method: Find disc center (Ra_disc, Dec_disc) by minimizing the imaginary part of continuum visibilities; fix center and calculate PA and inclination by minimizing dispersion of deprojected visibilities in circular annuli; measure 90% flux radius R_90% in concentric ellipses; compute dust mass from 1.3 mm flux.
assumptions: Dust opacity kappa_1.3mm = 2.3 cm^2 g^-1, dust temperature = 20 K, distance = 140 pc for targets without Gaia parallax, and low-resolution 1.3 mm fluxes used for total dust mass

recipe.goal: Extract deprojected radial brightness profiles and characterize substructures
recipe.method: Deproject CLEAN images to 0 deg inclination using fitted centers, PA, and inclinations; azimuthally average into radial brightness profiles; identify local minima (gaps), local maxima (rings), inner cavities (R_Cav, R_Cav.10%, 50%, 90%), central beam inner disc fluxes/masses, small cavities, and inflection points.
key_parameters: Azimuthal angles restricted to within 20 deg of the semi-major axis for highly inclined systems (ISO-Oph 37 and WSB 82); combined 0.03'' + 0.2'' image used beyond 1.0'' for WSB 82
assumptions: All features in a given disc share the same center, position angle, and inclination; inner disc dust mass uses T = 20 K and kappa_1.3mm = 2.3 cm^2 g^-1

recipe.goal: Reconstruct sub-beam radial profiles from visibilities using Frankenstein
recipe.method: Fit deprojected continuum visibilities directly using the non-parametric Gaussian process code Frankenstein (frank) to recover axisymmetric brightness profiles at sub-beam resolution and compare with CLEAN profiles.
assumptions: Azimuthal symmetry of the disc continuum emission

recipe.goal: Compare large-cavity disc profiles with planet-disc interaction and dust evolution simulations
recipe.method: Qualitatively compare observed 1.3 mm radial profiles of transition discs (WSB 82, DoAr 44, EM* SR 24S, RXJ1633.9-2442) with millimeter-sized dust surface density distributions at 0.5 and 5 Myr from numerical dust evolution models containing a giant planet.
key_parameters: 1 M_JUP planet at 70 au, alpha = 10^-3, fragmentation velocity threshold = 10 m s^-1, particle sizes 0.1-10 mm, evolution times 0.5 and 5 Myr

score_reason: Raw data and project codes are public, CASA and pipeline versions are explicitly stated, and visibility/profile analysis recipes and equations are clearly described and tabulated; minor deductions for missing self-calibration solints, TCLEAN cell/mask parameters, and frank hyperparameters.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA data are public under 2018.1.00028.S and 2016.1.00545.S, the imaging and radial profile analysis steps are straightforward to replicate, and the paper provides extensive numeric tables of disc geometry, fluxes, dust masses, and substructure locations/depths/widths.
